unit.title: Wait for the ground, then feed it
unit.needIt: Seeds planted too early rot and the money is gone. Knowing when the ground is ready saves you a whole wasted start.
unit.why: A gardener wants to plant seeds as soon as the sun comes out. However, the ground is still frozen and too wet for the seeds to survive. By waiting for the right weather, the gardener ensures the plants grow strong instead of dying in the cold.
unit.outcome: Wait for the right weather and soil conditions before starting your garden.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you wait for a sale to buy a good deal instead of buying something useless. You also feel it when you wait for a clear day to finish a big project at home.
unit.do: Check the local weather forecast for the next week. Look for a stretch of warm days to plan your first planting date.

quiz.q: What must happen to the ground before work can be done?
quiz.why: The frost needs to leave the ground so the soil can be worked.
quiz.quote: The frost must be allowed to get out of it, and after that an opportunity must be given for surplus water from melting snows and spring rains to drain away before work can be done to any advantage.

quiz.q: Why is it bad to plant seeds too early?
quiz.why: Early seeds often fail to sprout because of the cold.
quiz.quote: the gardener who is in too great a hurry often learns the truth which underlies the saying by the failure to germinate of the seed he puts into the ground very early in the season.

quiz.q: What does the saying 'one swallow does not make a summer' mean here?
choices: One warm day is not enough
quiz.why: A few warm days are not enough to guarantee the weather will stay warm.
quiz.quote: Read '' warm day"" for ''swallow"" and you will get the force of the statement.

quiz.q: What is the best manure for all kinds of vegetables?
choices: Old and well rotted barn-yard manure
quiz.why: The text states this is better than anything else for vegetables.
quiz.quote: Barn-yard manure, if old and well rotted, is better than anything else I have any knowledge of for all kinds of vegetables

quiz.q: Why do vegetables need extra food more than trees do?
quiz.why: Vegetable roots do not go deep, so they cannot find food on their own.
quiz.quote: The roots of most garden plants do not extend far in any direction, nor go very deep; therefore food must be given directly to them if we would secure the best possible result.

partials: Haste makes waste in the garden.
Frost must leave the ground first.
One warm day is not a summer.
Wait for growing weather to stay.
Vegetables need food given directly to them.
crystal.key: Good gardening requires waiting for the right conditions and providing direct nutrients.

decoys.text: Planting early makes plants grow faster.
decoys.why: The text says early plants are often damaged by frost and grow slower than later sowings.

decoys.text: Trees and vegetables need the same amount of manure.
decoys.why: The text explains that trees have deep roots and vegetables have shallow roots.

crystal.aha: By waiting for the right weather and feeding the shallow roots of vegetables, you ensure a healthy harvest.

scene.analogy: Painting a wall: wait until it is dry

actors.label: Rushing it means doing it twice.

beats.say: Paint on a wet wall peels off.
So you wait for it to dry.
Then you prime it, so the paint has something to hold.
Now the paint goes on and stays.
Seeds rot in cold wet ground. Wait, feed the soil, then plant.
